stories.title: Sonya Massey's killer Sean Grayson dies in US prison
stories.summary: Sean Grayson, the white US police officer convicted of murdering a black woman, Sonya Massey, during an incident at her home in 2024, has died in prison at age 32. Grayson shot dead Massey, 36, during an exchange that took place after she reported a suspected intruder at her residence in Illinois. The killing reignited the debate about police brutality in the US. Grayson said he fired because he thought Massey was about to throw a pot of boiling water on him. He was last year found guilty of second-degree murder. The former police officer was undergoing treatment for colon cancer. His lawyer Daniel Fultz confirmed to the BBC that Grayson had died on Sunday, but did not disclose the cause. The BBC has asked the Illinois Department of Corrections for comment. Lawyers for Massey's family said: "Grayson's death in custody from cancer does not bring Sonya back." "We wish his family prayers of peace, as we do for all who grieve a loved one. Sonya's family knows that pain all too well and will grieve her loss the rest of their days," the lawyers said, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner. Protests took place across the US in the aftermath of Massey's death, and then-President.

stories.title: Peskov recalls Putin’s remarks on grain situation
stories.summary: Dmitry Peskov refrained from discussing the commercial aspects
article_sentences: Grain intended for export will be shipped in full despite Kiev’s aggressive actions obstructing those exports, Russian President Vladimir Putin has said, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

At a briefing, the Kremlin spokesman was asked whether the president planned to hold a separate meeting on the situation in the agricultural sector, particularly grain exports, as well as about the current status of the grain hub project in Egypt.
"I will not discuss the commercial aspects.

I will only remind you that in his recent interview, the president mentioned that he had been in contact on this issue with both the prime minister and Agriculture Minister Oksana Lut, and that they discussed finding measures that would minimize the consequences of the difficulties we face as a result of the aggressive, unlawful conduct of the Kiev regime.
The measures have been identified, they will be worked out, and they will ensure the timely shipment of the grain intended for export in full.
That is what President Putin said," Peskov said in response to the question.
